title: People With Active Viremia Treated With Lenacapavir and Long-Acting Cabotegravir for Effectiveness
official: People With Active Viremia Treated With Lenacapavir and Long-Acting Cabotegravir for Effectiveness
summary: This pilot, single-arm, open-label study conducted in the United States will evaluate the efficacy, safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of long-acting lenacapavir plus cabotegravir (LA LEN+CAB) in people with HIV-1 viremia who have a history of non-adherence and confirmed or suspected rilpivirine (RPV) resistance. Participants will be on study for up to 108 weeks.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Documented HIV-1 infection
* Prior antiretroviral therapy (ART) experience, including having first been prescribed ART at least 24 weeks prior to enrollment and self-report of prior oral ART use
* HIV-1 RNA \>1000 copies/mL within 60 days prior to study entry
* Evidence of non-adherence to ART, including virologic failure, poor virologic response, or loss to clinical follow-up with ART non-use/non-adherence
* At least one reason why NNRTI-based ART is clinically inappropriate, including documented or suspected rilpivirine resistance or prior rilpivirine intolerance
* Adequate laboratory parameters within 60 days prior to study entry:

  * Absolute neutrophil count \>600/mm3
  * Hemoglobin ≥7.0 g/dL
  * Platelet count \>50,000/μL
  * AST and ALT ≤3 × upper limit of normal
  * Estimated glomerular filtration rate \>15 mL/min/1.73 m²
* For participants of childbearing potential, negative pregnancy test at screening and within 24 hours prior to study entry
* Ability and willingness to provide informed consent
* Connected to a medical clinic with access to HIV care and antiretroviral therapy

Exclusion Criteria:

* Documented integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI) resistance-associated mutations that may compromise cabotegravir activity
* Active hepatitis B infection, defined as positive hepatitis B surface antigen or detectable hepatitis B virus DNA
* Child-Pugh Class C cirrhosis
* No suitable injection site for cabotegravir administration due to implants, tattoos, or skin conditions interfering with injection site assessment
* Prior use of lenacapavir
* Receipt of HIV immunotherapeutic vaccines or HIV monoclonal antibodies within 6 months prior to study entry
* Serious medical or psychiatric condition
* Use of prohibited concomitant medications with lenacapavir or cabotegravir within 30 days prior to study entry
* Current pregnancy or breastfeeding
* Known allergy, hypersensitivity, or intolerance to cabotegravir, lenacapavir, or formulation components
sponsor: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)
